key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings with disk-like, highly spread droplets form denser microstructures and better long-term corrosion resistance, while higher humidity lowers friction and wear through tribochemical effects.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray parameters and controlling porosity can improve the durability of Fe-based protective coatings for steel components exposed to corrosive and humid service environments.
method: Detonation sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings onto Q235 carbon steel under different spraying parameters.
Compared droplet morphology, coating microstructure, corrosion behavior, and tribology performance.
Tested wear behavior across different humidity conditions with Si3N4 counterbodies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that coatings with higher droplet circularity and expansion factor had finer, denser lamellar structures, and that increased porosity correlated with poorer long-term corrosion resistance; friction coefficient and wear rate decreased as humidity increased.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on spray conditions and porosity control, so results may not transfer directly without process optimization for other substrates or environments.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
